headline: ME-VLM reports a unified embodied-agent model and lower M100 prefill latency
summary: The arXiv v2 paper presents ME-VLM, a model intended to combine embodied perception and action with multimodal agent planning and tool use. Its method trains separate agent and embodied experts, then distills them into one student with multi-teacher on-policy distillation. The authors report results on embodied, agent and transfer benchmarks. For M100 edge deployment, they report W4A8 quantization and visual-token reduction from 4,096 to 3,328 alongside prefill latency of 400 ms to 188 ms, with 96.7%/98.2% uncompressed-score retention for the 4B/35B models. These results are author-reported; this review did not reproduce them or establish broader end-to-end latency or power performance.
